title: Live rankings during a mock test
summary: Show 200,000 students their rank as a test ends, without the rush taking the system down.
context: Lalbagh Learning runs Sunday mock exams for 200,000 students. All of them finish within the same few minutes, and every one of them immediately refreshes to see a rank and percentile, overall and within their city.
Last Sunday, the results page took eleven minutes to appear. Some answers are also corrected after the test, when a question turns out to be wrong, and every rank must change.
must_handle: A student sees a rank within about a minute of the test closing.
Ranks are correct overall and within a city and a batch.
A student's own rank does not need the whole list to be read.
A corrected question recalculates everything without a long outage.
Refreshes in the first minutes do not reach the database each time.
show_in_answer: How scores are collected at the close.
How ranks are computed, stored and read.
What is cached and how the rush is absorbed.
What happens when a question is corrected.
